blocks.heading: From the first sip of tea to the last slow breath
blocks.body:
Every treatment is built around the same idea: enough time, gentle hands and products you can pronounce.

Tell us what you need when you book, or let us decide together at the door. Prices include the pot of tea and ten unhurried extra minutes.

items.question: Do I need to prepare for a facial?
items.answer: No. Arrive with clean or lightly made-up skin; we will cleanse it for you. Tell us about any allergies or skin conditions when you book.

items.question: Which massage is right for me?
items.answer: If you want to switch off, choose the warm stone massage. If you have a specific ache, choose deep tissue. If you are unsure, we will talk it through at the start and adjust as we go.

items.question: Can I bring a friend?
items.answer: Yes. We have two linked rooms for friends, couples and parents with grown-up children. Ask for a paired booking.

items.question: Are your products suitable for sensitive skin?
items.answer: Most are. We patch-test anything new on request, and we can leave out any ingredient you would like to avoid.

blocks.heading: Not sure what to choose?
blocks.text: Write to us and we will suggest a treatment for what you need this month.

pages.title: About
pages.description: The story and the people behind Maison Lune, a small fictional day spa.

blocks.heading: Our story
blocks.body:
Maison Lune began as one treatment room above a bakery on Harbour Lane, with a borrowed massage table and a very good kettle.

We believe that looking after yourself should feel like a small act of kindness, never a chore or an indulgence you need to apologise for. So we keep things simple: warm rooms, honest products, plenty of time.

Today we are four therapists, three rooms and still one very good kettle. Maison Lune is a fictional business, made up for this demonstration.

posts.title: Five small rituals for dry winter skin
posts.excerpt: Cold air and central heating are hard on skin. These five small habits make a big difference.
posts.alt: Amber bottles of massage oil on a wooden shelf
posts.body:
Winter is hard on skin. Cold air takes moisture out, and central heating takes out what is left.

## Five habits that help

- Wash with lukewarm water, never hot.
- Pat dry rather than rub.
- Moisturise while your skin is still damp.
- Add a few drops of facial oil at night.
- Drink water, and wear a scarf over your cheeks when it is windy.

None of these takes more than a minute. If your skin is still tight after a fortnight, come and see us: a short facial and some honest advice often does the trick.

> A little care, done often, beats a lot of care done rarely.

posts.title: What to expect at your first hot-stone massage
posts.excerpt: Smooth, warm and surprisingly gentle: here is what happens from the moment you arrive.
posts.alt: A tower of warm massage stones with a sprig of leaves
posts.body:
Hot-stone massage sounds dramatic, but it is one of the gentlest treatments we offer.

## Before you begin

We will ask about any aches, injuries or medications, and where you would like us to spend the most time. Then we leave the room while you settle under a warm blanket.

## During

The stones are smooth basalt, heated in water to a comfortable warmth. We place some along your back and use others in slow strokes, so the heat reaches the muscle underneath.

## Afterwards

Drink a glass of water and take your time getting up. Most people feel lighter, a little sleepy, and very hungry for toast.

posts.title: A pot of tea, three ways
posts.excerpt: The tea we pour after every treatment, and how to make it at home.
posts.alt: A bowl of water with floating petals
posts.body:
Every visit to Maison Lune ends with tea. These are the three we pour most often.

1. **Lemon verbena**: fresh leaves, hot water, five minutes. Bright and calming.
2. **Ginger and honey**: three slices of ginger simmered for ten minutes, with a spoon of honey.
3. **Roasted barley**: nutty and caffeine-free, lovely in the evening.

Use a pot if you have one, warm the cups first and, most importantly, sit down while you drink it.
